title: Adaptive warmup experiments (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a more resilient, adaptive warmup stage in throughput benchmarking runs. The goal: reduce variance introduced by insufficient priming while keeping wall-clock time reasonable for repeated CI/bench runs.

Context / motivation:
- We consistently see a 3–12% delta in steady throughput across runs depending on how priming sequences interact with KV cache and compilation kernels.
- Current fixed warmup periods are either overkill for short prompts or insufficient for long-context models. We need an adaptive algorithm that converges to a stable throughput window and records deterministic seeds for better repeatability.

High-level idea:
- Run a short incremental ramp. After each step sample a stability window (N samples) of tokens/sec and latency percentiles. Compute coefficient of variation (CoV = std / mean) over that window.
- Stop warmup when the metric(s) of interest reach stability thresholds for K consecutive windows. If not reached within max_warmup_time, mark run as "warmup-incomplete" and continue but tag results.

Metrics to consider during warmup (sampled at small fixed intervals, e.g., every 5s):
- tokens_per_sec (throughput)
- req/s (raw request rate)
- p50, p95, p99 latency
- GPU util, SM_efficiency, mem-bandwidth
- KV-cache-hit-rate (for cache-enabled experiments)
- model-compiled-flag (boolean: whether JIT/compilation completed)

Algorithm (pseudocode):
- params: sample_interval=5s, window_len=12 samples (~60s), cov_threshold=0.03, p95_rel_change_thresh=0.02, stable_required=2, max_warmup=900s
- windows_in_a_row = 0
- while elapsed < max_warmup:
    collect metrics for window_len samples (sleep sample_interval between)
    compute mean_tp, std_tp, cov = std_tp/mean_tp
    compute p95_change = abs(p95_current - p95_prev)/p95_prev (if p95_prev exists)
    if cov < cov_threshold and p95_change < p95_rel_change_thresh:
        windows_in_a_row += 1
    else:
        windows_in_a_row = 0
    if windows_in_a_row >= stable_required:
        warmup_done = true; break
- if not warmup_done: tag as warmup-incomplete

Rationale for chosen metrics and thresholds:
- CoV on throughput captures oscillations due to batching/occupancy fluctuations and is scale invariant across QPS levels.
- p95_rel_change guards against improvements from late compilation steps that improve tail latency without moving mean much.
- Requiring multiple consecutive stable windows reduces false positives from short lucky runs.

Sample loadgen config (conceptual):
- name: adaptive-ramp-01
  client_threads: 8
  target_qps: 0 (use ramp)
  ramp_strategy: stepped
  step_duration: 30s
  step_increment: +10 reqs/s
  request_payload: sample_prompt_set/v2.json
  seq_len_distribution: {short:40%, med:40%, long:20%}
  token_emit_mode: tokens (so we measure tokens/sec)
  rng_seed: 20240918-ash1
  kv_priming: true
  kv_priming_strategy: prefix-sampled  (see notes below)

Notes on priming sequences and KV cache:
- Two priming styles tried: 1) prefix-sampled: pick X realistic prefixes from eval set and emit them before measured requests; 2) rolling-prefix-stream: run a stream of full conversations until cache occupied.
- For Llama-like KV caches, a small number of long prefixes can prime key-value tables faster than many short ones (fewer unique positions). We should record priming sequence ids to reproduce later.

Repeatability checklist (to run before/after each benchmark run):
- Hardware: GPU model, driver, CUDA/cuDNN/nccl versions recorded.
- OS: kernel version, CPU governors, c-states disabled? (record actual settings).
- Container: image digest, runtime flags (RT_PREEMPT, cpuset).
- Model artifact: model hash, tokenizer hash, compile flags/quantization profile.
- Loadgen: config file used, rng seed, client version.
- Network: NIC offload settings, if using local interconnect record MTU and link speed.
- Background noise: scheduled cron jobs/monitoring agents paused?
- Log: capture full raw sample stream (time series) not just aggregates.

Post-run analysis steps:
1) Trim first warmup segment (if adaptive warmup declared done, mark warmup boundary timestamp). Keep full raw stream.
2) Compute sliding mean/std for tokens/sec with window 12 samples and produce CoV curve.
3) Compute tail-latency trends and mark any tail spikes aligned with GC/compilation events.
4) Correlate GPU SM efficiency changes with throughput dips (nvprof traces or metrics API).
5) Produce a small report with: steady_mean_tp, steady_p95, steady_p99, steady_CoV, warmup_time, was_warmup_successful.

Failure modes observed in experiments (notes):
- "Late compile" effect: first few windows show steadily improving p95 while tokens/sec climbs; where only CoV would not trigger stopping early. Need p95_rel_change check.
- "Cache thrash": when priming set contains many unique positions, cache insertions cause eviction and lower effective throughput. Using prefix-sampled set with fewer unique position ids helps.
- "Batching oscillation": aggressive client-side concurrency + autoscaler pairing sometimes oscillates batch sizes. Add a small jitter to client request interarrival times (uniform ±5%) to avoid pathological sync.

Lightweight heuristics we tried (and outcomes):
- heuristic: stop after two windows where tokens/sec improves <1% and p95 change <1% -> outcome: stable for short prompts but missed late-compile for long-context models.
- heuristic: require extra verification window after model-compile event -> outcome: caught late improvements but extended warmup time ~+120s on average.

Operational knobs to expose in harness config:
- sample_interval and window_len (tradeoff granularity vs time)
- cov_threshold and p95_rel_change_thresh (sensitivity)
- max_warmup_time (safety limit)
- priming_strategy + priming_seed_ids (to make priming deterministic)
- jitter_pct for interarrival times

Commands used during exploration (examples):
- run loadgen: ./bin/loadgen --config configs/adaptive-ramp-01.yaml --outdir /tmp/run-20240918 --log-stream raw_stream.csv
- collect GPU counters: python infra/collect_gpu_metrics.py --job run-20240918 --interval 5s --out gpu_metrics.csv
- annotate traces: ./infra/annotate_trace.py --trace nsight_run.qdrep --events raw_stream.csv --out annotated.html

Quick experiment log (notes from 2024-09-20):
- experiment A: 1xA10G, batcher=dynamic, priming=prefix-sampled(8), sample_interval=5s, window_len=12
  - warmup_time: 78s, steady_tokens_sec: 32.8k, CoV: 0.028, p95: 120ms
- experiment B: same but priming=rolling-prefix-stream
  - warmup_time: 210s, steady_tokens_sec: 30.3k, CoV: 0.045, p95: 170ms -> indicates cache thrash
- experiment C: A10G but added client jitter ±5%
  - steady_tokens_sec: 33.1k, CoV: 0.025, fewer tail spikes

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Decide standard default thresholds (cov_threshold, p95_rel_change) for CI runs vs long-form lab runs.
- Add extraction of "model-compile" event from runtime logs and tie into warmup algorithm more directly.
- Create a small library to encode priming sequences (id -> prefix list) so experiments can share and declare exactly which priming was used.
- Try adaptive warmup with Poisson arrival distribution (not stepped/ramped) to mimic some production patterns.

Appendix: recommended minimal metadata to store with every run (CSV-friendly columns):
- run_id, start_ts, warmup_end_ts, warmup_duration_s, steady_mean_tp, steady_p50_ms, steady_p95_ms, steady_p99_ms, steady_CoV, gpu_model, driver_version, model_hash, priming_strategy, rng_seed, warmup_status, notes

End of scratchpad.

(If this looks useful I'll formalize into a playbook with example YAML configs and a small helper to re-run exact priming sequences.)
